variants.headline: The treasury slips into deficit
body: The treasury has slipped into deficit. Spending outruns income by {{deficit}} gold a season, where the last count held the books at balance or better, and the gap repeats each season until it is closed.

variants.headline: The books, newly behind
body: Last count: the books at balance or better.
This count: the books behind.
Behind by: {{deficit}} gold, every season.

variants.headline: A bill that comes back every season
body: The treasury is spending {{deficit}} gold a season more than it takes in. Sell a piece of public land and the proceeds might cover this season's bill. At the current rate, the same bill comes due next season, with one piece of land fewer to sell. Any minister who proposes a sale should bring next season's figures too.

variants.headline: Sir, the treasury now outspends its income
body: I keep a stall by the east gate. When I spend more than I take, my wife hears of it before the market closes, and the week after there is no honey on the table. The treasury now spends {{deficit}} gold a season more than it takes. Who at the palace hears of it, and what goes missing from their table?

variants.headline: The treasury passes a thousand gold
body: The treasury has crossed the thousand-gold mark. It stands at {{gold}} gold, up {{gain}} gold since the last count. At the public pay window, a supplier waiting to collect asked how much of that money was already spoken for.

variants.headline: The reserve passes the thousand mark
body: It is a pleasure to record that the treasury has passed the thousand-gold mark and now holds {{gold}} gold, a store grown by {{gain}} gold in recent seasons. A full vault is the mark of a well-kept house, and of stewards who keep their counts before their comforts.

variants.headline: Hear it! A thousand gold in the vault!
body: Hear it, merchants and magistrates, hear it! The treasury has passed the thousand-gold mark and holds {{gold}} gold in the vault. A thousand gold and more, counted and kept, counted and kept!

variants.headline: The treasury just crossed 1,000 gold
body: Reserve: {{gold}} gold. Up {{gain}} gold over the last few seasons. The thousand mark is behind us, and the number is exact.

variants.headline: The treasury gains time against the deficit
body: The treasury can stretch its reserve further even though it still runs a deficit. At the current shortfall of {{deficit}} gold a season, its {{gold}} gold can cover {{turnsLeft}} full seasons.

variants.headline: What the treasury can do with more time
body: At a shortfall of {{deficit}} gold a season, the treasury now has enough in reserve for {{turnsLeft}} full seasons. That gives ministers time to collect money already owed before they have to consider a new tax in a hurry. The advantage lasts only while receipts and spending hold near today's figures.

variants.headline: The count runs long at the money-changer's table
body: Not long ago, the money-changers were counting the treasury's remaining seasons on their fingers, and nobody liked the total. This morning the tally at the table ran to {{turnsLeft}} seasons of cover, {{gold}} gold against {{deficit}} a season, and the talk over the coins came easier. The oldest of them still kept his coat on. Habits.

variants.headline: The treasury reserve runs short
body: The deficit continues at {{deficit}} gold a season, and the reserve behind it is thinning. The {{gold}} gold on hand will cover {{turnsLeft}} more seasons of spending at that rate.

variants.headline: The treasury, counted
body: The vault holds: {{gold}} gold.
The court spends beyond its income: {{deficit}} gold a season.
At this rate the vault answers for {{turnsLeft}} seasons, and no more.

variants.headline: Treasury cover: {{turnsLeft}} seasons left
body: The treasury holds {{gold}} gold tonight. Spending outruns income by {{deficit}} gold a season. That leaves {{turnsLeft}} seasons of cover, and the shortfall is not new. What nobody in the palace has said is what happens when the count reaches zero. We asked. There was no answer yet.

variants.headline: The old rule was a full store
body: Our grandparents kept a store against bad years, and the bad years came all the same. The treasury holds {{gold}} gold against a deficit of {{deficit}} gold a season, and that is {{turnsLeft}} seasons from empty. The old rule was plain: a full store first, arguments after. Fill it now, while there is still something to fill it from.

variants.headline: The deficit ends
body: The treasury has returned to surplus. Income again covers spending, with {{goldPerTurn}} gold a season to spare where the recent count showed a shortfall.

variants.headline: The state pays its way
body: The books are back in the black: the treasury now clears {{goldPerTurn}} gold a season after the recent shortfall. Spending no longer outruns income, and the state is lending to its own future rather than borrowing from it.

variants.headline: Notice: the accounts no longer run behind
body: Notice is given that the deficit lately showing in the accounts has closed. The rate now reads {{goldPerTurn}} gold a season to the good, a correction made without panic. Good order in the treasury serves the whole nation, and the ministers concerned merit its thanks.

variants.headline: The purse that stopped leaking
body: They say a stopped leak is the first gold in the purse. The treasury's leak has stopped.

variants.headline: Hear it! The lean stretch is over!
body: Hear it, good people, hear it! Income now beats spending by {{goldPerTurn}} gold a season, and the deficit is done with! The lean stretch is behind us, behind us!
